title: Hire people who give a shit: Alexandr Wang's hiring screen at Scale
summary: Alexandr Wang explains that after interviewing every Scale offer, he screens for two things: caring about the company's mission and caring about work in general. He warns against becoming a credential brand, argues recruiting should feel like courtship, and shares his interview questions for spotting obsession.

principles.text: Screen for two things: they care about the company, and they care about their work in general.
principles.quote: I mainly screen for one key thing: giving a shit. To be more specific, there’s actually two things to screen for:

principles.text: Caring doesn't guarantee great work, but not caring guarantees bad work, so mission fit is non-negotiable.
principles.quote: While it is not guaranteed that someone who gives shit will do great work, it is guaranteed that they will not do good work if they do not give a shit.

principles.text: As a company grows, more candidates come for the brand; more top-of-funnel hides a sharp drop in hire ROI.
principles.quote: it will be more common for people to interview for the brand rather than the substance. In fact, most growing companies often miss this effect entirely, and simply observe the fact they’re getting far more top-of-funnel.

principles.text: Recruit like courtship, not a college admissions office; look for people you'd want beside you through long nights.
principles.quote: A recruiting team that looks like a college admissions office is certain death for a startup. If you’re built to simply sift through a swarm of homogeneous candidates, then on the other side you will simply get a higher credentialed homogeneous soup.

principles.text: Past obsession predicts future obsession; probe how hard they've worked and why they cared.
principles.quote: If someone is applying to Scale and has never been deeply obsessed about something before, then it’s a bad bet to think Scale will be the first.

principles.text: Culture is the people and their effort, not perks or office cosmetics.
principles.quote: No perk tells me anything meaningful about the company, other than how comfortable with spending money they are. The company _is_ the culture.
